notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a SerialDriver (family serial, family-config), but the wire protocol is framed, not a line of text - '#' + address + sequence + '?VR'/'VS' + parameter id + instance + parameter + CRC16 XMODEM + CR (FisbaReadyBeam/__init__.py:160-193, 125-136) - and the class builds and checksums each frame at run time, so a SerialDriver command table cannot reproduce it; this is a direct Driver over FisbaReadyBeam:FisbaReadyBeam with a native.py factory. NOT COVERED: the only reads are the device status (parameter 104) and the device type (parameter 100, returned as the raw response frame, not the parsed 1171); brightness is write-only - the upstream class has no getter for the power parameter 7013, so the resource state reports the last value written and after an e-stop it still shows the last commanded brightness while the native call has switched all channels to 0 (the read cannot show the native safe state); the actual laser powers, the digital-control state (parameter 7000), the channel switch (parameter 7006) and the any-laser-on query (parameter 7010) are not read back - the last one is only printed by the upstream debug path. The class does not validate the brightness value; the 0 to 100.5 percent bound comes from the set_brightness docstring (line 203) and the code that treats a power not > 0 as off (lines 210-213), and the runtime enforces it before the native call. The clone states no laser safety class and no hardware interlock, so the site's laser safety measures stay authoritative and no hardware interlock is modelled; risk stays at the card floor R1. The fake is an in-memory stand-in with placeholder values, not a recording: the clone has no simulator and no hardware was available, so the card's preferred transcript could not be recorded. driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null: the package is model-authored and unreviewed, and nothing in it ran on hardware. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits: risk raised from R1 to R2 (a laser module above class 1; a class 3B or 4 module is R3, MHS/spec/04-safety.md), so the hardware backend waits for a human signature; native.py and facts.md now say so. The reviewer added the safe-state action x-cap.complight.lasers_off.v1 (the e-stop's native call) as the independent stop G3 asks for at R2. The DEVIATION FROM THE CARD is accepted: a registry override now makes the card a direct driver. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
